open_points.subject: owner-session concurrency
open_points.text: A session holds at most one: showing a confirmation step replaces the one pending (M11).
open_points.question: When concurrent owner requests show confirmation steps or otherwise change the same session state, in what order are they applied and which pending confirmation survives?
options: Serialize all requests that change one owner session
Use completion order
Use arrival order without otherwise serializing the requests
open_points.default_guess: Serialize changes to each owner session and let the later serialized request replace the pending confirmation.

open_points.subject: in-flight request after sign-out
open_points.text: a request that passes it completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs
open_points.question: If that completing request would create or replace session-bound state such as a confirmation or uploaded file after a concurrent sign-out has ended the session, is that state discarded, recreated, or allowed to survive?
options: Complete the business action but discard new session-bound state
Allow the request to restore or retain session-bound state
Cancel any session-state effect while allowing non-session effects to commit
open_points.default_guess: Let already-authorized non-session effects complete but discard any session-bound state because the session has ended.

open_points.subject: confirmation binding digest
open_points.text: kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order, never as the values themselves
open_points.question: Which digest algorithm, value encoding, normalization and fixed field order define equality of confirmation-bound inputs?
options: Digest a specified canonical encoding of typed values
Digest the exact submitted bytes
Leave each action to define its own encoding
open_points.default_guess: Use a release-fixed cryptographic digest over a length-delimited canonical encoding and an explicitly declared field order.

open_points.subject: showing a confirmation step
open_points.text: Every change in the owner interface carries the CSRF protection bound to its session ... showing a confirmation step replaces the one pending
open_points.question: Because showing a confirmation step changes the session by replacing its pending value, must the request that shows the step itself pass CSRF protection?
options: Yes, showing the step is a session-changing request
No, only the eventual confirmed submission needs CSRF
Only replacement of an existing confirmation needs CSRF
open_points.default_guess: Require CSRF protection whenever showing the step creates or replaces pending confirmation state.

open_points.subject: audit-entry eligibility
open_points.text: An entry is written by an accepted action that changes state ... An accepted action that changes nothing ... writes no entry, but for the erasure of old audit entries
open_points.question: Does an accepted erasure of old audit entries that removes no prior entry satisfy A14's entry-writing rule despite not changing pre-existing state?
options: Yes, make it an explicit exception to rule 1
No, write no entry when nothing is removed
Treat writing its own entry as the state change
open_points.default_guess: Make audit erasure an explicit exception to rule 1 and always write its entry.

open_points.subject: confirmation id for an empty audit erasure
open_points.text: A confirmation id is minted only for an accepted, confirmed action that changes state ... An erasure that removes no entry still writes its own entry ... with its confirmation id
open_points.question: When an accepted audit erasure removes no old entry, is a confirmation id minted?
options: Mint it because audit erasure is an explicit exception
Do not mint it, leaving its entry without a confirmation id
Refuse an erasure that would remove nothing
open_points.default_guess: Mint and record the confirmation id for every accepted audit erasure.

open_points.subject: malformed project at upload
open_points.text: answers ... each project the file holds with its id and status ... A file that cannot be read ... or that holds two project records with one id, is refused whole at upload
open_points.question: What happens at upload when a syntactically readable project record lacks an id or status, so it cannot be displayed or selected, but is not one of the two stated whole-upload refusal cases?
options: Refuse the whole upload
Keep the file and display an unselectable malformed record
Ignore that project unless another record refers to it
open_points.default_guess: Refuse the whole upload because Registry cannot construct the required project mapping.

open_points.subject: import during owner-only restore
open_points.text: right after it Registry makes a backup run outside the daily schedule ... an owner-only start makes no run
open_points.question: May the owner repeat a lost import while the restored instance is in owner-only mode, and if so does the mandatory post-import backup run despite the owner-only prohibition?
options: Allow the import and allow its exceptional backup run
Allow the import but defer backup until service-token mode
Refuse import until service-token mode
open_points.default_guess: Allow the import in owner-only mode and allow the import-triggered backup as a narrow exception.

open_points.subject: retained import reconstruction data
open_points.text: the owner keeps the export file and the picks, names and aliases given in the import until a checked backup holds the import
open_points.question: Does the retained recovery material also have to include every Customer mapping input required by A16—kind and whether the v1 value is the tax id—or must the owner decide those again after a restore?
options: Retain every confirmed mapping input
Retain only the explicitly listed picks, names and aliases
Permit the owner to choose new Customer mapping values on re-import
open_points.default_guess: Retain every input bound to the accepted import confirmation, including Customer kind and tax-id choice.

open_points.subject: missing store at startup
open_points.text: When the store's configured file does not exist and its directory does, Registry makes a new, empty store
open_points.question: How does Registry distinguish an intentional first installation from a lost, deleted or wrongly configured production store that must be restored under R0-89?
options: Require an explicit initialization flag or separate initialization operation
Always create an empty store and rely on the owner to notice loss
Require a persistent installation marker outside the store
open_points.default_guess: Require explicit initialization authority before creating an empty store; otherwise fail startup as a missing store.

open_points.subject: same-day backup after import
open_points.text: Besides the run after an accepted import ... at most one backup is made per UTC day ... right after it Registry makes a backup run outside the daily schedule
open_points.question: If the day's daily backup already succeeded before an import, is a second post-import backup made, is the earlier backup replaced, or is the import-triggered run skipped?
options: Allow a second backup that day after import
Replace the earlier same-day backup
Skip the post-import backup until the next day
open_points.default_guess: Allow the exceptional post-import backup in addition to the earlier daily backup.

open_points.subject: backup encryption format
open_points.text: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key ... A backup records, readable without its key, its instant, the release ... and a digest of the key
open_points.question: Which authenticated-encryption scheme, nonce handling, key derivation, file format and authentication coverage—including whether the clear metadata is authenticated—define a valid backup?
options: Specify a versioned authenticated-encryption envelope covering ciphertext and metadata
Encrypt only the store bytes and leave metadata unauthenticated
Delegate the format entirely to the selected dependency
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned authenticated-encryption envelope with unique nonces and authenticate all clear metadata as associated data.

open_points.subject: last backup-run status
open_points.text: The owner interface shows ... whether the last run failed
open_points.question: Where is the last-run result kept, and after a restart does 'last run' mean the last attempted run before the restart or only a run in the current process?
options: Persist every run result in the store
Keep it only in runtime state and show unknown after restart
Derive success from backups and persist failures separately
open_points.default_guess: Persist the last attempted run's instant and outcome so the interface remains truthful across restarts.

open_points.subject: request-id validity
open_points.text: each carry a request id: an opaque value the caller makes ... A create without a request id is refused
open_points.question: Is an empty or whitespace-only request id considered present, and what format, length or entropy limits must request ids satisfy?
options: Define a nonblank bounded opaque string
Require a UUID
Accept any present value, including empty text
open_points.default_guess: Require a nonblank, bounded opaque identifier and have Registry-generated owner-interface values use cryptographic randomness.

open_points.subject: audit-erasure recovery record
open_points.text: the latest date audit entries were erased by ... a governance document ... naming each action by its date, kind and the customer_ref or project_id it touched
open_points.question: For an audit-erasure action, which touches neither a customer nor a project, where is the cutoff date needed to repeat the erasure after restore recorded, and is it distinct from the action's date?
options: Record the cutoff date as an action-specific value
Treat the action date as the cutoff date
Do not repeat audit erasures after restore
open_points.default_guess: Record the supplied audit cutoff date explicitly and separately from the date on which the action was performed.

open_points.subject: uploaded files in other owner sessions
open_points.text: at most one uploaded import file ... dropped when the import is accepted ... a file another session keeps stays until that session ends
open_points.question: When one session accepts the import, are uploaded files in every other owner session dropped or do they remain until those sessions end?
options: Drop only the confirming session's file
Drop every session's uploaded import file
Keep other files only until their next request
open_points.default_guess: Follow A16's specific rule: drop only the confirming session's file and leave other sessions' files until replacement or session end.
